analysis.plain_explanation: You received a legal notice because your cheque for Rs 80,000 bounced due to a low balance. Under the law, you have a limited time of 15 days from receiving the notice to respond or clear the payment. Since you want to pay in instalments, you should contact the supplier in writing before this deadline expires to propose an instalment plan. If the supplier agrees, get the agreement in writing to avoid legal action. If you ignore the notice or fail to pay within the time limit, the supplier can file a formal complaint in court. Since legal deadlines are strict, you should consider consulting a lawyer to help draft a reply.

draft_document.text:
To,
[SUPPLIER OR ADVOCATE NAME]
[SUPPLIER ADDRESS]

Date: [DATE]

Subject: Reply to legal notice dated 2 November 2026 regarding bounced cheque for Rs 80,000

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am in receipt of your legal notice dated 2 November 2026 regarding the cheque of Rs 80,000 issued to you, which was returned by the bank on 25 October 2026 due to low account balance.

I acknowledge the debt owed for the goods purchased. Due to temporary financial difficulties, I was unable to clear the full amount immediately. However, I am willing to clear the dues in instalments and request your cooperation in this matter.

Kindly confirm if you agree to an instalment plan so that we can settle this amicably.

Yours sincerely,

[YOUR NAME]
[YOUR CONTACT INFORMATION]
